'''Pierre Agostini''' ({{IPA|fr|pjɛʁ aɡɔstini}}; born 23 July 1941) is a French [[experimental physics|experimental physicist]] and [[Emeritus]] professor at the [[Ohio State University]] in the United States, known for his pioneering work in strong-field laser physics and [[attosecond science]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Agostini |first1=Pierre |last2=DiMauro |first2=Louis F |date=1 June 2004 |title=The physics of attosecond light pulses |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0034-4885/67/6/R01 |journal=Reports on Progress in Physics |volume=67 |issue=6 |pages=813–855 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/67/6/R01 |bibcode=2004RPPh...67..813A |s2cid=250879086 |issn=0034-4885|url-access=subscription }}</ref> He is especially known for the observation of [[above-threshold ionization]] and the invention of the [[reconstruction of attosecond beating by interference of two-photon transitions]] (RABBITT) technique<ref>{{Cite web |last=Garisto |first=Daniel |title=This Year's Physics Nobel Awards Scientists for Slicing Reality into Attoseconds |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/this-years-physics-nobel-awards-scientists-for-slicing-reality-into-attoseconds/ |access-date=2023-10-04 |website=Scientific American |language=en}}</ref> for characterization of [[Attosecond physics|attosecond]] light pulses. He was jointly awarded the 2023 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last1=Edwards |first1=Christian |last2=Hunt |first2=Katie |last3=Upright |first3=Ed |date=October 3, 2023 |title=Nobel Prize in physics won by trio who created rapid flashes of light to 'capture the shortest of moments' |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2023/10/03/europe/nobel-prize-physics-electrons-flashes-light-intl-scn/index.html |work=[[CNN]]}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Pierre Agostini was born in [[Tunis]], in the [[French protectorate of Tunisia]], in 1941.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |date=1970 |title=Contributors [Back cover] |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/xpl/tocresult.jsp?isnumber=23203 |journal=IEEE Journal of Quantum Electronics |volume=6 |issue=12}}</ref> He obtained his ''[[baccalauréat]]'' at the [[Prytanée national militaire]] school in 1959 in [[La Flèche]], France.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 October 2023 |title=Prix Nobel de physique 2023 : l'un des lauréats, Pierre Agostini, a obtenu son baccalauréat au Prytanée de La Flèche |url=https://france3-regions.francetvinfo.fr/pays-de-la-loire/sarthe/le-mans/prix-nobel-de-physique-2023-l-un-des-laureats-pierre-agostini-a-obtenu-son-baccalaureat-au-prytanee-de-la-fleche-2849696.html |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=France 3 Pays de la Loire |language=fr-FR}}</ref>
[[File:Photograph_of_Professor_Pierre_Agostini_giving_a_lecture_at_Swinburne_University_Sarawak_Campus.jpg|alt=Pierre Agostini delivering a lecture|thumb|Agostini delivering a lecture at Swinburne University of Technology Sarawak Campus.]]
Agostini studied physics at [[Aix-Marseille University]], where he subsequently received a [[Bachelor of Education|B.Ed.]] degree (''licence d'enseignement'') in physics in 1961, and an [[Master of Advanced Studies|M.A.S.]] degree (''diplôme d'études approfondies'') in 1962. In 1968 he completed a [[doctoral degree]] there, on multilayer dielectric filters for the ultraviolet, titled ''Appareillage permettant la réalisation de filtres multidiélectriques UV : Étude des couches Sb<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub>''.<ref name="phd">
{{cite thesis |type=PhD |publisher=[[Aix-Marseille University]] |publication-place= |last=Agostini |first=Pierre |date=1967 |title=Appareillage permettant la réalisation de filtres multidiélectriques UV : Étude des couches Sb<sub>2</sub>O<sub>3</sub> cryolithe |oclc=491622236 |hdl= |doi= |osti= |url=https://catalogue.univ-amu.fr/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=633261 }}
</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3" />

After his doctorate, he became a researcher at [[CEA Paris-Saclay|CEA Saclay]] in 1969 and stayed there until 2002.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">
{{cite web |url=https://dokumen.tips/documents/p-agostini-biography-department-of-agostini-biography-pierre-agostini-professor.html |title=Ohio State University, Department of Physics: P. Agostini Biography |last= |first= |date= |website=dokumen.tips |publisher= |access-date=2023-10-09 |quote=}}
</ref> During this time, Agostini worked in the lab of Gérard Mainfray and Claude Manus, where he researched on multiphoton ionization using the powerful lasers there. They are the first to observe [[above-threshold ionization]] in 1979 in [[xenon]] gas.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mainfray |first1=G |last2=Manus |first2=C |date=1 October 1991 |title=Multiphoton ionization of atoms |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0034-4885/54/10/002 |journal=Reports on Progress in Physics |volume=54 |issue=10 |pages=1333–1372 |doi=10.1088/0034-4885/54/10/002 |bibcode=1991RPPh...54.1333M |issn=0034-4885|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Agostini |first1=P. |last2=Fabre |first2=F. |last3=Mainfray |first3=G. |last4=Petite |first4=G. |last5=Rahman |first5=N. K. |date=23 April 1979 |title=Free-Free Transitions Following Six-Photon Ionization of Xenon Atoms |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=42 |issue=17 |pages=1127–1130 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.42.1127|doi-access=free |bibcode=1979PhRvL..42.1127A }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=D'Oliveira |first1=Pascal |last2=Carré |first2=Bertrand |date=2010 |title=Dossier : Les lasers à l'IRAMIS: Les lasers de puissance à Saclay |script-title= |url=https://iramis.cea.fr/Comm/2010laserIRAMIS/laser_puissance_historique.php |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=IRAMIS |language=fr |archive-date=5 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231005040724/https://iramis.cea.fr/Comm/2010laserIRAMIS/laser_puissance_historique.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In 2001, Agostini and his team at CEA Saclay along with Harm Geert Muller at the Dutch Foundation for Fundamental Research on Matter (FOM), using an advanced laser at the {{ill|Laboratoire d'Optique Appliquée|fr}}, managed to create a train of pulses each 250 [[attosecond]]s in duration. By recombining the ultrashort [[ultraviolet]] pulses with the original [[infrared]] light they created an interference effect that allowed him to characterize the length and repetition rate of the pulses.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 October 2023 |title=Pierre Agostini, Ferenc Krausz and Anne L'Huillier win 2023 Nobel Prize for Physics |url=https://physicsworld.com/pierre-agostini-ferenc-krausz-and-anne-lhuillier-win-2023-nobel-prize-for-physics/ |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=Physics World |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Paul |first1=P. M. |last2=Toma |first2=E. S. |last3=Breger |first3=P. |last4=Mullot |first4=G. |last5=Augé |first5=F. |last6=Balcou |first6=Ph. |last7=Muller |first7=H. G. |last8=Agostini |first8=P. |date=2001 |title=Observation of a Train of Attosecond Pulses from High Harmonic Generation |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1059413 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=292 |issue=5522 |pages=1689–1692 |doi=10.1126/science.1059413 |pmid=11387467 |bibcode=2001Sci...292.1689P |issn=0036-8075|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Agostini was a visiting scientist at the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] in the U.S. state of [[New York (state)|New York]] between 2002 and 2004, where he worked in [[Louis F. DiMauro]]'s group.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Palm International School of Attosecond |url=https://iramis.cea.fr/meetings/PISA/lecturers.php |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=IRAMIS |language=fr |archive-date=4 October 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231004102255/https://iramis.cea.fr/meetings/PISA/lecturers.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> He became professor of physics at the [[Ohio State University]] (OSU) in 2005 and ran a laboratory jointly with Louis F. DiMauro who moved a year earlier to OSU.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pierre Agostini – Emeritus Professor, Ohio, USA {{!}} eMedEvents |url=https://www.emedevents.com/speaker-profile/pierre-agostini |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=www.emedevents.com}}</ref> Agostini became emeritus professor at OSU in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jeremy Pelzer |first=cleveland com |date=3 October 2023 |title=Ohio State University retired professor wins 2023 Nobel Prize in Physics |url=https://www.cleveland.com/news/2023/10/ohio-state-university-retired-professor-wins-2023-nobel-prize-in-physics.html |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=cleveland |language=en}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
Agostini received the Gustave Ribaud prize in 1995 from the [[French Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014 |title=Prix Gustave Ribaud |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_ribaud10.pdf |website=Académie des Sciences |access-date=3 October 2023 |archive-date=24 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231224101445/https://www.academie-sciences.fr/archivage_site/activite/prix/laureat_ribaud10.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 2003, he received the [[Gay-Lussac–Humboldt Prize]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Liste des lauréats français du prix Gay-Lussac Humboldt|language=fr|url=https://media.enseignementsup-recherche.gouv.fr/file/2010/22/0/Liste-laureats-francais-prix_Gay-Lussac-Humboldt_136220.pdf}}</ref> and the Joop Los fellowship from the Dutch Foundation for Fundamental Research on Matter (FOM),<ref name=":1" /> he also received the [[William F. Meggers Award in Spectroscopy]] in 2007 from the [[Optica (society)|Optical Society of America]] (OSA), and is a [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Humboldt Fellow]]. He was elected a Fellow of OSA in 2008 “for leadership in the development of innovative experiments providing major insights into the dynamics of the nonlinear response of atoms and molecules submitted to strong infrared laser pulses.”<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Pierre Agostini – Professor, Ohio, USA {{!}} Optica |url=https://www.optica.org/history/biographies/bios/pierre_agostini/ |access-date=3 October 2023 |website=www.optica.org}}</ref>

In 2023, he received the Nobel Prize in Physics for "experimental methods that generate attosecond pulses of light for the study of electron dynamics in matter" along with [[Anne L'Huillier]] and [[Ferenc Krausz]].<ref name=":0" />
